The '''1972–73 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|70th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|41st consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

== Summary ==
The club finished a disappointing fourth in the league five points behind champions [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist6979.html|title= La Liga 1972–73|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation}}</ref> Meanwhile, in the Copa del Generalísimo the team was eliminated early in the round of 16 by [[Sporting Gijón]], losing the away game 0–1 and achieving a miserable draw 1–1 at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arandaarquitectos.com/websporting/index72.html|title=Temporada 72–73 Sporting Gijón|publisher=arandaarquitectos.com|language=Spanish}}</ref>

During February [[Santiago Bernabéu (footballer)|Santiago Bernabéu]] visited [[Israel]] and gave a medal to [[Moshe Dayan]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/opinion/2014/05/21/blogs/1400662800_1089745.html|date=21 May 2014|access-date=31 August 2021|title=A medal from Bernabeu to Moshe Dayan|language=Spanish|publisher=as.com}}</ref> a gesture which strained relations with [[Francisco Franco]] and becoming crucial to deny further government support for a new stadium project.

The squad reached the semi-finals of the European Cup where it was defeated twice by the defending champions and future winners [[AFC Ajax|Ajax Amsterdam]] who would go on to repeat their success in the following season, making it three in a row.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2018/10/26/why-ajaxs-european-cup-triumph-in-1973-was-met-with-fan-disgruntlement-as-their-fate-loomed-large/|title=Why Ajax's European Cup triumph in 1973 was met with Fan disgruntlement as their fate loomed large|publisher=thesefootballtimes.co}}</ref> President Santiago Bernabéu attended the [[1973 European Cup Final|Final]] himself expecting to sign Ajax starplayer [[Johan Cruyff]] who instead was ultimately signed by archrivals [[FC Barcelona|CF Barcelona]] during the summer transfer window.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/02/13/5c6422a1268e3e2d598b4598.html|title=Why did Cruyff not Sign for Real Madrid?|publisher=Diario Marca|date=13 February 2019|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> Real Madrid's offer for the Dutchman was reported to be significantly higher, but he refused to play for the club linked to Franco and his regime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportscafe.in/football/articles/2016/mar/25/johan-cruyff-the-dutchman-who-stood-up-for-catalonia/|title=Johan Cruyff – The Dutchman who stood up for Catalonia}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2017/09/27/real-madrid-and-the-franco-regime/|title=THE STORY OF REAL MADRID AND THE FRANCO REGIME}}</ref>
